turns.t: Yeah, g'day. Look, I'm not really sure why I'm here, the kidney lady said to come and see you. Something about my numbers going down.
No worries. Do you remember which numbers, or what she said they meant? ~
Nah, not really. Just that the kidney one's been dropping over the last few tests. I didn't ask a lot of questions, to be honest. ~
That's all right, I've got the results here, and I'll explain them. First, how have you been feeling? ~
Tired, mostly. Dragging myself around. It's been like that since the winter, I reckon.
Anything else that you've noticed? ~
My ankles puff up by the end of the day, my socks leave marks.
Both ankles?
Both, yeah. Though the left's a bit worse.
Have you noticed any blood in your urine, or has it been frothy?
No blood. It's bubbly sometimes, I suppose, but no blood.
Do you get up at night to pass water more than before? ~
Once, maybe twice. About the same as always. ~
Anyone in the family with kidney trouble?
My mum. She ended up with kidney failure, around sixty. She was on dialysis for a bit before she passed.
I'm sorry. That's helpful for me to know. Any trouble with your breathing?
No, my breathing's fine.
Okay, I'm going to have a look at you. Can you pop up on the bed? ~
Sure. ~
Press here, does that pinch? I'm checking your ankles.
Nah, no pain. ~
There's mild swelling around both ankles, a bit more on the left, and when I press it leaves a dent.
Is that the kidneys? ~
It can be, it's a sign the body's holding on to fluid. Now your chest, deep breath in. ~
In. ~
Your lungs are clear. Good.
What's your thinking, doc? ~

The kidney number, called the eGFR, is lower than it should be and it's been falling. With the tiredness and swelling, I can't rule out something blocking the flow of urine, though a slow, long-term kidney problem is more likely.
Right. And what do we do? ~
I'd like to arrange a kidney ultrasound, to look at their size and check there's no blockage.
Is that the jelly on the belly? ~
That's the one. And I'd like a urine test to look for protein. You'll collect a sample in the morning.
Easy. ~
Try to eat less salt, because it makes the ankles swell, and put your feet up in the evenings.
Salt. Okay. I do love a pie. ~
Maybe fewer pies. If the swelling spreads up your legs, or you start passing much less urine, come back sooner.
Right. I'll do that. ~
I'll have the results to go over with you when they're back. ~
Thanks, doc. ~
